newsitem.title: UK: US, Canadian institutions seen seeking hedge funds.
newsitem.headline: US, Canadian institutions seen seeking hedge funds.

text.p: U.S. and Canadian institutional investors are showing increasing interest in "macro" hedge and futures funds, despite a decline in returns from the high levels of the late 1980s and early 1990s.

A report from Global Fund Analysis, a trading name of TASS Management Ltd, said "the managers of some of the better performing funds report a desire on the part of some institutional investors to diversify away from traditional stock and bond markets, which they see as fully valued".
The last time they showed any interest was in 1993 but the heavy losses sustained by many hedge funds in the 1994 bear market then scared them off.
"Since then returns have recovered, but not to their previous levels," the report said.

Managers believe discretionary funds should perform well in the next few years relative to traditional equity and debt funds but there is still a question mark over the record of "systematic" funds, which are managed with the aid of computer systems.
Global Fund analysis said it was becoming easier for U.S. and Canadian institutions to buy macro hedge funds because regulations were easing in both countries.
